one: Computer graphics in the AI era: neural rendering, differentiable rendering, materials/textures, animation, and physics simulation.
pos: CS 348I discusses how deep learning is changing four areas of graphics: rendering, geometry, animation, and imaging. For each problem it presents the classical solution first, then SOTA learned methods, and critically evaluates results and impact — a good fit for graphics + AI.
topics: **Differentiable/neural rendering**: NeRF, Gaussian Splatting, neural rendering
**Materials and lighting**: BRDF estimation, inverse rendering
**Textures and images**: texture synthesis, denoising, super-resolution, shading
assess: Programming assignments plus a project. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: Graphics, rendering, 3D generation, and film/game technology.
tips: Brush up on graphics fundamentals (ray tracing, BRDF, rendering equation) first. Pair with CS 348N/CS 468.
note: Not offered in the 2026–27 ExploreCourses listing; no stable course-site link found.
